title: Fruits Basket -prelude-
summary: An 88-minute TMS theatrical film (JP 2022-02-18) built in three acts: a clip show recut from the 63-episode 2019-2021 TV run, then the film's real body — the Kyoko-and-Katsuya story — then a short epilogue of Tohru and Kyo after the series. The chapters are stated outright by the production, not inferred: TMS producer Genki Ito, interviewed by Febri, says 「今回、今日子と勝也のエピソード（原作第90話〜第93話）を映像化するにあたり…」 — the film animates the owner's manga chapters 90-93, the four-chapter flashback that opens volume 16 (en-WP's chapter list: Volume 16 = 'Chapters 90-95', and its volume summary is that flashback beat for beat; Hakusensha's own vol-16 copy calls it 「感動の勝也&今日子編!!」). Those four chapters are the one block the TV run never adapted: Ito says that when they first structured the 63 episodes 「今日子と勝也の話を入れることができなかったのが心残りでした」, director Yoshihide Ibata says on the official site that they deliberately kept Katsuya's face off-screen during the TV series because the film was already greenlit (「実はTVシリーズでは勝也の顔をわざと出さないようにしていたんです」), SlashFilm describes the team having 'chose[n] to cut out Kyoko and Katsuya Honda's love story from the anime series', and the fandom's per-episode chapter fields jump from ch 88-89 (ep 48, 'It's Cinderella-ish') straight to ch 94-95 (ep 49, 'Here You Are') with 90-92 named by no episode at all — only ch 93's closing present-day frame was relocated into ep 57. Sizing (two independent reviews): the clip show runs ~30 minutes, with the title card at the 33-minute mark; the adaptation of ch 90-93 is 'the last hour', 'a loyal adaptation of the story, which is basically ripped from the manga pages'; the Takaya-written epilogue 'lasts three minutes'. Under T28's recap clause the clip show is weightless and the remainder decides — ~52 minutes of faithful source adaptation beside a 3-minute coda — so the standing is canon on ch 90-93. The surprise: even that coda is not studio-original — Takaya drew it herself as a 16-page epilogue manga handed to filmgoers on opening day (ANN 2022-01-21: 'a 20-page booklet with a 16-page epilogue manga story newly created by Takaya… The film also recounts the same epilogue story'), so the film contains no studio-invented story at all.

chapters_adapted.note: The Kyoko-and-Katsuya flashback that opens vol 16, animated in order and in full: ch 90 (Kyo's first recollection of Kyoko; her delinquent past and meeting student teacher Katsuya Honda), ch 91 (Katsuya gets her out of her abusive home and proposes), ch 92 (the marriage, Tohru's birth, three happy years, Katsuya's sudden death), ch 93 (Kyoko's grief, the near-suicide, her choice to live for Tohru). Named as 原作第90話〜第93話 by the film's own producer (Febri) and corroborated by the fandom's chapter pages (all four = vol 16, 31+30+31+31 = 123 pages) and en-WP's volume-16 summary. Share: ~52 of the film's 88 minutes (the 'last hour' after the 33-minute title card) — 123 pages at ~2.4 pages/min, i.e. the same page rate as the TV run's own ~2 chapters per 24-minute episode, which is what a full, unhurried adaptation looks like. FIRST-TIME MATERIAL, not a duplicate: ch 90-92 appear in no episode of the 63-row run, and of ch 93 only the closing present-day frame (Kyo's nightmare of Kyoko and his mother, the hamburger scene) was relocated into ep 57 'That's Right, It's Empty' — the Kyoko flashback body inside ch 93 is animated here for the first time. NOT counted in this range: the ~30-minute opening clip show (re-cut TV footage; see recap) and the ~3-minute Takaya-written epilogue, which is after the manga's ending and carries no chapter number.

position.why: CONFIRMED at 63.5 — directly after ep 63 'See You Again Soon', the TV finale. The chapter-order slot would be 48.5: the film's ch 90-93 sit exactly between ep 48 (ch 88-89) and ep 49 (ch 94-95) in the fandom's per-episode fields, which is where a reader following the manga meets this flashback. But the work cannot be watched there. Its first act is a ~30-minute clip show of all three seasons, ending — per SlashFilm — on 'Kyo and Tohru visiting Kyoko's grave, looking to the future together', a post-confession, post-finale scene; and its last act is a 3-minute epilogue set after the series ends (ANN news: the same story as the bonus booklet, 'the story after [Tohru and Kyō]'). Placed at 48.5 the film would spoil the confession, Kyo's confinement, the curse breaking and the ending, roughly fifteen episodes early. 63.5 is also the release slot (2022-02-18, eight months after the finale) and matches how the production framed it: the official site's INTRODUCTION and STORY describe only the Kyoko/Katsuya story, and the producer's account has the epilogue written specifically to tie the film back to the finished series. Recommended note for the display, since the two facts differ: 'watch after ep 63; the chapters it adapts (90-93) fall between eps 48 and 49'.

flags_for_sean: THE STANDING FORK, SIZED — canon (delivered) vs mixed. Runtime split, from two independent professional reviews: recap ~30 min and the title card at the 33-minute mark (But Why Tho: 'it isn't until the 33-minute mark that the title card comes up, and the real story can begin'; 'an uneven recap takes up a third of it'; ANN: 'The first half hour of the movie is a clip show'), source adaptation of ch 90-93 ~52 min ('The last hour of the film is where its beauty is'), Takaya's epilogue ~3 min (ANN: 'it lasts three minutes'; the official site's Yuma Uchida: 透と夾のその後も『ちょっとだけ』描かれています). I ruled canon on T28's RECAP CLAUSE (Sean 2026-09-02, FotNS 130): a clip show counts for NOTHING and you judge the remainder — pure source adaptation → canon — and 'never let a recap's SIZE make a row mixed' (FotNS 130 was a 9m28s clip show inside a 24-minute episode, i.e. a LARGER share than this film's third, and it stayed canon). Read literally, PROTOCOL-extras' line 'New footage with source content inside a recap → mixed' plus N8 would make it mixed; the two rules meet head-on here because the recap is a whole act. My reason for preferring canon beyond the rule text: the recap is not this work's job. The official site's INTRODUCTION and STORY describe ONLY the Kyoko/Katsuya story, the film exists because chs 90-93 would not fit in the TV structure (producer, Febri), and the remaining non-recap minute is the author's own coda, not studio invention. If you want the compilation reading instead, the row is `mixed` with the same chapters, the same position and the same recap note.

KIND: I left the stored kind as `movie` and set `recap: true` (a compilation is PART of the work, per N8's 'say recap: true and name what it compiles'). What it compiles: ~30-33 minutes re-cut from the 2019-2021 TV run's 63 episodes, arranged around Kyo's point of view and his guilt over Kyoko's death, ending on Kyo and Tohru at Kyoko's grave. One caveat on 'no new footage in act one': SlashFilm records a single newly animated scene inside the recap — Kyo's first meeting with Kyoko — which is itself ch 90's opening beat, so even the recap act's only new footage is source material. Say if you want kind repaired to `recap`; I do not recommend it (two thirds of the film is new animation).

THE EPILOGUE HAS A PRINTED FORM — a decision you may want, though it does not change this standing. The 3-minute coda is 高屋先生原案 (producer, Febri) and Takaya drew it as manga: a 16-page epilogue story inside the 20-page booklet given to every filmgoer from 2022-02-18 (ANN 2022-01-21 — 'The film also recounts the same epilogue story'), plus an 8-page Takaya manga in the June BD (en-WP). That is almost certainly AniList 147825 'Fruits Basket: prelude - Special Comics', the second MANGA edge on this work. Under T26 I recorded NO adoption: 高屋奈月's credit here is 原作・総監修 (official site STAFF) and a same-day tie-in booklet is not the author writing the film's events into the serialized source line; a screenplay/original part that exists only as the film is a credit, never an adoption. But the booklet may deserve its own related-work / chain node decision, and it is the fact that makes canon comfortable: this film contains no studio-invented story.

OWNER-LEVEL OBSERVATION, NOT RESEARCHED (do not act on it from this verdict). Building the full coverage set from the fandom's 63 per-episode `chapter` fields, four other chapters are named by no episode: 110, 112, 113, 133. Those are more likely field DROPS (the known fandom trap) than skips — unlike 90-92 they have no licensor or producer statement behind them, and the producer's stated aim was 最初から原作を全部アニメ化する ('animate the whole manga from the start', Febri part 2). Worth a look whenever the owner's run is anchored; today the run carries no chapter anchors at all.

IF THE RUN IS EVER ANCHORED, this verdict hands you two free fence facts, both two-source: ep 48 'It's Cinderella-ish' ends at ch 89 and ep 49 'Here You Are' starts at ch 94, so the run's own continue across that seam skips 90-93 — the film is what fills it (C3-style skip note: 'read ch 90-93 with the film, or after ep 63'). And ep 57 'That's Right, It's Empty' carries a relocated share of ch 93 (its present-day frame) alongside ch 115/117/118 — a `rearranged` shape, not a second adaptation of the flashback.
